_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematics P1 (algebra, patterns, functions, finance and probability), November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, nine compulsory questions (Q1 27, Q2 19, Q3 9, Q4 14, Q5 17, Q6 16,

questions.context: 9.3 During the summer season in South Africa, the probability of sunny weather on any given day is 0,7. If it is sunny, the probability that a person uses sunscreen is x. If it is not sunny, the probability of using sunscreen is 0,2x.
questions.text: Draw a tree diagram, clearly labelling the branches and indicating the outcomes.
questions.topic: Probability: tree diagrams and contingency tables
questions.memo_answer: First branches: sunny S 0,7 and not sunny S' 0,3. From S: uses sunscreen U x, not U' 1 - x. From S': U 0,2x, U' 1 - 0,2x. Outcomes: SU 0,7x; SU' 0,7(1 - x); S'U 0,06x; S'U' 0,3(1 - 0,2x).
